messages:
mia: Heads-up — got several alerts overnight. OTEL gateway started dropping ~12% of incoming traces from the eu-west GPU fleet between 03:10 and 03:40 UTC. Appears correlated with a spike in high-cardinality tags (gpu_id + job_id) and tail-sampler DB timeouts.

raj: Ugh. Did we see any OOMs on the gateway during that window? :eyes:

jules: No OOMs on the gateway pod logs, but tail-sampler Redis RT was spiking to 700ms and some requests timed out. I can paste logs.

jules: ```
2026-03-12T03:12:05Z gateway[pid=72] WARN tail-sampler: lookup timeout for trace_id=... key=tail:project:eu-west
2026-03-12T03:12:08Z gateway[pid=72] ERROR exporter/http: 504 Gateway Timeout while flushing sampled span
```

cassie: We pushed a change last week that added `gpu_node` and `batch_id` to span attributes for debugging model routing. That increased cardinality a lot for short-lived jobs. Might be the catalyst.

mia: Confirmed — trace samples with `gpu_node` go through for a long time (lots of unique values). We didn't cap or hash them.

raj: We need to balance observability vs cost. If tail-sampling needs Redis lookups per trace and cardinality explodes, costs and latency blow up. Suggest: 1) drop `gpu_node` from span tags at runtime 2) enable head-based sampling at runtime with a conservatively low rate 3) move to redis hypertable or sampled tail store. Thoughts?

infra-sre: +1 to dropping gpu_node in _all_ spans. We can add a sanitized attribute `gpu_region` with low cardinality instead. Also recommend making tail-sampling async fallback: if redis lookup >200ms, treat as unsampled (or use head-sample decision).

trace-gateway-bot: Incident note — gateway autoscaler kicked at 03:15 UTC (scale from 3 -> 6) due to CPU surge. No pod restarts.

cassie: Proposed quick config patch (runtime SDK):
```yaml
processors:
  batch:
  attributes/transform:
    - action: update
      key: gpu_node
      new_value: "{{ split(gpu_node, '-') | first }}" # reduce cardinality to region prefix
samplers:
  probabilistic:
    sampling_fraction: 0.001
```
This would collapse the GPU id into region prefix and set a low head-sample rate.

jules: For gateway tail-sampler config, we can add a size-based guard and fallback: if pending traces > 1000 then bypass tail-sampling and head-sample at 0.1%. Also need to tune Redis pool size.

mia: Action items: 
- cassie to rollout attribute transform to strip gpu_node full id -> due today EOD
- jules to add fallback to tail-sampler + increase redis pool temporarily -> ASAP
- raj to update Grafana panel to show trace-insert latency, tail-sampler queue depth, and unique tag cardinality by hour -> tomorrow morning
- infra-sre to confirm autoscaler threshold isn't too aggressive for bursts -> today

raj: I'll create a tiny dashboard patch. We should correlate trace drops with GPU provisioning events (scale up/down) so we can see if node churn is a factor.

mia: Also note cost impact: traced tokens/ingest in backend spiked ~18% that window. If this becomes common, we'll need sampling policies per customer tier.

ops-bot: Scheduled job "otel-gateway-config-backup" completed at 04:00 UTC.

cassie: I pushed a PR with the attribute transform and a short note on why we collapse IDs. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-config/pull/422 :thumbsup:

jules: After the patch, let's run a 2h synthetic load against eu-west to validate tail-sampler behavior and watch unique tag cardinality in prometheus.

mia: Good plan. If we see improvements, follow-up: plan an adult migration to tail-based sampling with storage-tiered lookups (redis -> db) and stricter cardinality controls for any runtime-added tags.

raj: FYI I'm adding an alert that fires if trace-drop-rate > 1% for 10m and tail-sampler redis latency > 200ms.

mia: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread as you roll things out. :v:
